All three theoretical deepenings, their examples and scope distinctions retained
No changes to recursive closure thesis, remainder two-sidedness or relativity to organizing principle
No added theoretical debate or compressed summary
Shared historical corrections limited to existing paragraphs

Persons-as-ends distinguished from a guaranteed historical destination, not stripped of normative meaning
English suggestions each match once in original and sequential application

coverage: I: Two theoretical cores; recursive closure impulse; Sedition Act, post-WWI Red Scare, McCarthyism and Japanese American internment; suppression/absorption boundary argument and initial old-age-insurance example; Louisiana Purchase, parties, territorial expansion, slavery and Indigenous dispossession; full synthesis of two-sidedness.

II: Comparative-history bounds; Madison's political pessimism, separation/checks as design premise, contrast with sister series, non-perfect machine, three implications; Civil War and Reconstruction now explicitly distinguish continuity of inquiry from absence of rupture.

III: Founding universalism and enslaved/Indigenous/women's exclusion; three anti-fatalist claims, durable enforcement versus unsupported automaticity, PATCO's political reversal with distinct legal regime, and inexhaustible but unguaranteed universalism.

IV: Jackson, Lincoln, Theodore Roosevelt, New Deal, Cold War and Nixon expansion sequence; excluded versus overgrown-power remainders, military-industrial complex, distributed/selective checking and lawful reorganization; 1937 adjustment, Watergate contingency/tape, legitimacy costs and Iran-Contra rebound.

V: Declaration, Gettysburg, Fourteenth/Fifteenth, Seneca Falls/Nineteenth and civil-rights sequence; auctioned enslaved person, excluded Black voter and interned Japanese American; persons as ends retained as persistent remainder rather than inevitable historical telos.
VI: China/Hundred Schools conservation comparison; Eurasian/Augustan formal-versus-substantive contrast with authorization and rebound; closure moments, delayed repudiation and unrepaired harms.

VII: All three theoretical feedback claims preserved, including acknowledged non-closure as design premise and public channels; universal two-sidedness versus context-specific closure-as-remainder; organizing-principle relativity fully retained.

VIII: Return to cycle rather than national celebration; one case does not prove law; end-of-history illusion and 2000 procedural outcome without consensus; repeated and reversible openness, all three parallel channels and final continuing-cycle cadence.

items: Closure constraints and executive rebound are possibilities requiring action, not automatic corrections.
Initial contributory old-age insurance coverage, not the whole Social Security system, was roughly half the workforce.
Public conflict channels do not confer immunity from Civil War and rupture; institutions were remade through war and Reconstruction.
Rights require durable enforcement and continuing political/judicial support; PATCO's federal strike ban is distinct from Wagner's private-sector coverage.
Internal administrative consolidation remains subject to congressional authorization and statutory limits, despite selective effectiveness of checks.
Mutual adjustment is a demonstrated response, not the only crisis outcome; correction/repudiation can arrive late and cannot erase harm.
Persons-as-ends is not an inevitable destination of history; theoretical framework unchanged.
Openness belongs to the design ideal and repeated political struggle, can be lost, and was never uninterrupted.

ep26.en.reason: Package note: First Red Scare and Palmer raids after the war.

ep26.en.old: It cannot make conflict disappear; neither can it make the desire to make conflict disappear.
ep26.en.new: It cannot make conflict disappear; neither can it eliminate the desire to do so.

ep26.en.old: The New Deal absorbed half the workforce into social insurance while simultaneously drawing the line that excluded the other half.
ep26.en.new: The New Deal's initial contributory old-age insurance covered roughly half the workforce while drawing a line that excluded much of the rest.
ep26.en.reason: Bound coverage to initial contributory old-age program, not all social insurance.

ep26.en.old: Second, this premise is what allowed the process of gradual inclusion — tracked across twenty-five essays — to continue without the catastrophic periodic ruptures that end the closure-seeking structures.
ep26.en.new: Second, this premise helped sustain and reopen channels for inclusion across the history tracked in these essays. It did not prevent catastrophic rupture: the Civil War makes that impossible to claim. The distinction is a capacity to reconstruct channels for conflict and inclusion, not immunity to their collapse.
ep26.en.reason: Do not erase Civil War; preserve design-premise contrast without immunity claim.

ep26.en.old: The declaration of equality does not extend itself to anyone;
ep26.en.new: The declaration of equality does not automatically extend to everyone;
ep26.en.reason: Restore Chinese distinction: no automatic universal fulfillment, not benefit to nobody.

ep26.en.old: Second: inclusion is not guaranteed — it can hold or be reversed, and its durability depends entirely on whether it has been translated into self-executing institutional machinery rather than left dependent on political goodwill. The Fifteenth Amendment failed because it relied on sustained federal will; the 1965 Voting Rights Act held (for decades) because its preclearance mechanism made federal oversight automatic rather than discretionary.
ep26.en.new: Second: inclusion is not guaranteed — it can hold or be reversed, and its durability depends in part on whether rights are supported by lasting enforcement mechanisms. Reconstruction had constitutional and statutory guarantees, but their implementation could be hollowed out when federal commitment weakened. The 1965 Voting Rights Act's preclearance mechanism reduced dependence on a new federal response to each discriminatory rule; it did not remove the need for political and judicial support.
ep26.en.reason: Align with EP22: law existed during Reconstruction; preclearance is not self-executing beyond politics.

ep26.en.old: Reagan's dismissal of the air traffic controllers — the federal hand that had protected organized labor since the Wagner Act visibly withdrawn — demonstrates that absorption is not a ratchet.
ep26.en.new: Reagan's dismissal of air traffic controllers who refused to return to work symbolized a withdrawal of federal protection for organized labor. These were federal employees subject to a legal strike ban, not private-sector workers covered by the Wagner Act. The political reversal, despite that legal distinction, demonstrates that absorption is not a ratchet.
ep26.en.reason: Clarify PATCO's legal regime and retain symbolic reversal.

ep26.en.old: Each expansion eventually triggered the structure's institutional self-correction.
ep26.en.new: Such expansion could trigger institutional self-correction, but its timing and effectiveness depended on choices by particular people and institutions; it was never guaranteed.

ep26.en.old: American expansions have typically required ex post legislative ratification, have tended to contract after emergencies, and have consistently faced institutional rebound.
ep26.en.new: American expansions have often sought subsequent legislative approval, have sometimes contracted after emergencies, and have encountered important episodes of institutional resistance.
ep26.en.reason: Avoid uniform retrospective authorization, contraction or rebound.

ep26.en.old: The American structure displays the cycle differently: the remainder develops continuously and publicly, the structure adjusts repeatedly without rupture, the crisis is endemic rather than catastrophic.
ep26.en.new: The American case reveals another possibility within the cycle: institutions can provide channels for the remainder to develop continuously and publicly, making repeated adjustment possible. That possibility coexists with violent rupture, above all the Civil War; it is not a guarantee that crises remain manageable.
ep26.en.reason: Open channels coexist with rupture; retain alternative mode.

ep26.en.old: That is all it ever does, and all it needs to do: produce a provisional outcome from which the next round can begin,
ep26.en.new: This shows one crucial function of its procedures: to produce a provisional outcome from which the next round can begin,
ep26.en.reason: Do not add exclusive normative claim that provisional procedure is the state's only duty.

ep26.en.old: Its greatness is not that it solved anything. It is that it has remained open — open to the knocking of the excluded, open to the rebound against overgrown power, open to each generation's renewed contestation of what the state is for.
ep26.en.new: Its greatness is not that it has solved everything or remained open without interruption. It lies in a capacity for reopening, won repeatedly through struggle — open to the knocking of the excluded, open to the rebound against overgrown power, open to each generation's renewed contestation of what the state is for.
ep26.en.reason: Qualify uninterrupted openness; retain conclusion's three parallel channels.

ep26.en.old: The cycle continues because the structure holds, and the structure holds because it has never asked the cycle to stop.
ep26.en.new: The cycle continues as the structure survives and is rebuilt; its constitutional design offers resources for keeping the contest open, even though successive generations must struggle to make that promise real.
ep26.en.reason: Design ideal is not uninterrupted historical practice.
